transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-03
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Torres (Aperture - Head of ML), Sara Nguyen (Aperture - Platform Eng), Rashid Khan (Aperture - CTO)

Summary: quick demo of Redwood Optimize console, live cost sims, and recommendations for prefix caching and KV cache prefetching tailored to Aperture's product recommendation workload.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side. Omar and I will run through an Optimize session — focusing on batching, prefix/KV cache, and a couple of cost scenarios for your recs workload. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Liam Torres: Liam here. Sorry, running late, grabbed coffee. We mostly want to see how we can shave token spend and keep p99 < 300ms.
[00:20] Sara Nguyen: Sara from infra, curious about VPC and logs.
[00:25] Rashid Khan: Rashid, CTO — interested in pilots and security checks.
[00:30] Omar Patel: great, thanks. Quick context check: Liam, you mentioned 300ms p99 for recommendation endpoint and ~3M requests/day in peak? Is that still the ballpark?
[00:39] Liam Torres: yea, rough peak. avg prompt length is 40 tokens, completions ~80 tokens, but distribution is heavy tail — some longer sessions when customers browse. Also we have short multi-turn flows for personalization.
[00:54] Omar Patel: perfect. That distribution matters for batching and KV cache efficiency. If most requests share a common prefix — like user context + item features — prefix caching can reuse KV cache across requests and drop inference work.
[01:08] Sara Nguyen: can you explain difference between prefix cache and KV cache? our eng folks sort of conflate them.
[01:15] Omar Patel: sure — in Redwood lingo: prefix cache is a higher-level optimization that stores computed prefix tokens (hidden states) keyed on deterministic prompt prefixes. KV cache is the lower-level transformer key-value cache used for autoregressive generation. We expose both concepts in Optimize: prefix caching is an application-level hint; the runtime leverages KV cache under the hood. Sorry if the docs say KV cash sometimes, transcription gets weird.
[01:38] Liam Torres: so if we precompute prefix for product+user context, we can serve completions faster with smaller compute per request?
[01:44] Omar Patel: exactly. Two common patterns: prefetch (proactive compute) where you warm the KV cache for anticipated items, and on-demand prefix caching which stores prefix latent states keyed by user/item hash.
[01:58] Maya Chen: we prepared three cost scenarios in the console — baseline (no caching), moderate (prefix cache with 30% hit rate), and aggressive (prefetch + KV with 65% hit). We'll walk the cost model and throughput charts.
[02:12] [screen share noise]
[02:20] Omar Patel: demoing Optimize console now — on the left are workload histograms, tokens per request, and the simulator. Here you can toggle batching window (ms), max concurrent inflight, and whether to enable prefix cache. See how latency percentile shifts.
[02:36] Sara Nguyen: so what does batching window mean operationally?
[02:39] Omar Patel: it's the small wait time that groups requests into one GPU call. Longer windows increase batching (lower cost/token) but add tail latency. For your p99 target we recommend 4-6ms window with concurrency cap of ~80 for the dedicated pool sizes you quoted.
[02:55] Liam Torres: 4-6ms seems small; are there diminishing returns? our traffic is spiky.
[03:01] Omar Patel: yes, diminishing returns past ~12ms. For spiky traffic we pair window tuning with autoscale policies — short burst capacity so you don't exceed latency SLO during traffic bursts.
[03:12] Rashid Khan: curious about dedicated vs hosted here — pilot we'd probably want hosted to start, but we need data residency and audit logs.
[03:20] Maya Chen: hosted first is common, and we can enable audit exports and region pinning. If you need VPC or private plane later, we can migrate to Dedicated/Private with same configs.
[03:30] [small crosstalk]
[03:36] Omar Patel: back to cache models — here's the cost delta. Baseline shows $0.018 per 1k tokens (example), moderate drops to $0.012, aggressive to $0.007 when KV cache hit rate is high and batching is tuned. Big caveat: hit rate assumptions must match your prompt uniqueness.
[03:55] Liam Torres: our prompt uniqueness is... moderate. We have a long tail of unique user/item combinations but top 3k SKUs represent 45% of traffic.
[04:06] Omar Patel: ideal for prefix cache — if you precompute prefixes for that top segment, you capture big cost savings. We'll simulate with your SKU distribution if you can share traces.
[04:16] Sara Nguyen: what about memory footprint of prefix cache? worried about GPU RAM and eviction.
[04:22] Omar Patel: good point — Optimize shows estimated KV memory per cache entry; we can cap prefix cache size in the config, and runtime uses LRU with eviction and spill-to-SSD options for Dedicated.
[04:34] Liam Torres: spill-to-ssd? isn't that slow?
[04:37] Omar Patel: it's slower than GPU RAM but still much faster than recomputing full prefix — useful for cold entries. For strict latency targets it's better to restrict cache to top hot keys.
[04:49] Maya Chen: Omar, can you show the simulated p99 chart when we enable prefetch for sessions that hit a predictive signal?
[04:55] [short pause]
[05:00] Omar Patel: toggling prefetch — see the darker blue line at p99 dropping from 420ms to ~270ms in this scenario. Cost per token also drops because fewer tokens are recomputed.
[05:12] Sara Nguyen: that drop is promising. How do we estimate engineering cost to implement prefetching in our infra?
[05:18] Maya Chen: typical tasks — adding a small async worker that predicts next items (could be existing recs model), calling Redwood prefetch API to warm KV cache, and instrumenting traces. Redwood has an SDK + sample worker in the docs.
[05:33] Liam Torres: what's the rollout risk? if prefetch doesn't match real traffic, do we waste compute and raise cost?
[05:40] Omar Patel: yes, prefetch false positives cost cycles. Optimize has a simulation mode that models prefetch accuracy and shows net cost delta. For pilot we recommend conservative thresholds and A/B deploys.
[05:53] Rashid Khan: security red flags for us are SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration for encryption at rest. Also SOC2 and ISO.
[06:01] Maya Chen: we are SOC2 Type II, support customer-managed KMS for Private, and for Hosted we offer envelope encryption plus audit export. I'll attach the security pack.
[06:12] Liam Torres: cool. Also curious about fallback behavior — if KV cache misses, do we have graceful degradation?
[06:18] Omar Patel: yes, runtime falls back to compute and can route to a smaller cheaper model variant or to a cached approximate response depending on your route policy.
[06:27] [audio artifact — brief silence]
[06:34] Omar Patel: jumping back to numbers — we ran a synthetic sim with your average tokens and top-3k SKU hit. With moderate batching and prefix cache at 35% hit rate, cost down ~42% and p99 at 290ms. We'll replicate with your traces for accuracy.
[06:53] Liam Torres: okay, pilot scope then? what do you recommend for a 2-week pilot?
[07:00] Maya Chen: Pilot scope: 1) integrate Redwood SDK + prefetch worker (engineering), 2) share 72h traces and allow Redwood to run simulated scenarios, 3) enable Optimize recommendations and run A/B for 2 endpoints. We'll provide benchmarks and a cost workbook.
[07:17] Sara Nguyen: do you need production credentials for traces?
[07:20] Maya Chen: preferably we'll work with anonymized traces in S3 or BigQuery. Also we can do live test traffic with a feature flag.
[07:28] Rashid Khan: timeline — we can commit infra people for two weeks mid-Dec.
[07:33] Liam Torres: sounds good.
[07:36] Omar Patel: quick note on metrics to watch: per-request compute tokens, KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency, GPU utilization, and tail latency. Optimize dashboard has those charts by route.
[07:52] Sara Nguyen: is there a toggle for autoscale behavior during holiday spikes?
[07:57] Omar Patel: yes, policy-based autoscale with burst credits. We'll draft suggested autoscale policy based on your concurrency curve.
[08:06] [short crosstalk]
[08:12] Maya Chen: wrapping up — recap and next steps.
[08:16] Maya Chen: Action items: Maya to send cost model workbook and security pack, Omar to run a focused sim (prefetch + KV) and upload results, Liam to share anonymized prompt traces. Then schedule pilot kickoff — propose Dec 10.
[08:31] Liam Torres: Dec 10 works for us.
[08:34] Sara Nguyen: We'll prepare S3 share and some infra notes.
[08:37] Rashid Khan: we'll review the security pack.
[08:41] Maya Chen: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invite and docs.
[08:45] [meeting ends]

Notes about transcription quality: several nouns misrecognized (KV cash, prefetch spelled various ways), but technical content is intact. References: cost workbook link (will be attached in follow-up), Optimize console demo recording (link forthcoming).
